newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says Afghan chief Dostum asks for help.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says Afghan chief Dostum asks for help.

text.p: Turkey said on Wednesday that Afghan warlord Abdul Rashid Dostum, his forces locked in a standoff with the Islamist Taleban militia, had asked Ankara and other capitals for diplomatic and political help.
"There are continuous requests to us as well as other countries from General Dostum for diplomatic and political support," foreign ministry spokesman Omer Akbel said.
Akbel said Turkey was in contact with Dostum through its consulate in the far northern town of Mazar-i-Sharif, controlled by the ethnic Uzbek leader.
He said he was unaware of Dostum asking Turkey for military aid. "As far as I know, there has been no such request."
Dostum met foreign ministry officials on a trip to Turkey in 1994.

Tanks, heavy artillery and multiple launch Grad missiles of Dostum's forces were dug in at both ends of the vital Salang tunnel northwest Kabul on Wednesday, but one of his commanders said there had been no fighting with nearby Taleban forces.
Dostum, who controls much of north Afghanistan, had distanced his forces from fighting between the Taleban and the former Kabul government, which fell last week.
